To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adoption of Twitter profiles by Italian municipalities is still limited and unevenly distributed across the country.

the Italian municipalities’ Twitter profiles are unevenly distributed in the country, with the most populated areas being more active, and that the profiles are mainly used for information dissemination rather than for interaction with citizens.

• Twitter is used by only a few municipalities (about 10% of the 8,000 municipalities in Italy); • the diffusion of Twitter in Italian municipalities seems to follow a spatial distribution pattern which is similar to the spatial distribution of the Italian municipalities’ population; • the municipalities that are most likely to adopt Twitter are the ones with a high level of digital literacy and a tradition in the use of social media; • the most active Twitter profiles are the ones of the small and medium-sized cities

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Italian municipalities have not yet fully exploited the potential of social media to improve their governance, but that the phenomenon is growing and that there are some good practices which could be adopted by other municipalities.
the adoption of social networking tools by public administrations is still in its early stages.

the Italian municipalities are still at the beginning of the journey in the use of social networking tools, but the potential of these new technologies to enhance e-parti- cipation, e-democracy and e-govern- ance is already being recognized and is starting to be implemented.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of social networking tools for communication purposes is not yet widespread in Italy.

, in order to achieve the goals of the new public communication, public administrations should be able to manage a plurality of communication channels, and should also be able to evaluate and monitor the performance of the communication tools in terms of the quantity and quality of the interactions with the public.
the use of these technologies is not a panacea for public communication but it is a tool which can be used to improve the quality and the quantity of information shared with the public.
